title: Canonical scalar shifts transport coherent line towers
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $S$ a scheme, and $L_0\subseteq L_1\subseteq L_2$ finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, allowing repetitions [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_i=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L_i,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_{ji}=-\otimes^L_{R_i}R_j$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $\alpha:C_{21}C_{10}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{20}$ be the ordinary derived tensor associator [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], and let $s_{ji,K,n}:C_{ji}(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{ji}K)[n]$ be the canonical comparison induced by termwise change of rings, with cochain convention $P[n]^r=P^{r+n}$ and differential $(-1)^n d_P$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
For every K-flat flat-term complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], $s$ is represented by the identity $P^{r+n}\otimes R_j\to(P\otimes R_j)[n]^r$ on tensor components. It is natural in all derived morphisms and satisfies, for every $K\in D(R_0)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$,
$$s_{20,K,n}\circ\alpha_{K[n]}=\alpha_K[n]\circ s_{21,C_{10}K,n}\circ C_{21}(s_{10,K,n}).$$
For any objects $K_i\in D(R_i)$ and isomorphisms $w_{ji}:C_{ji}K_i\xrightarrow{\sim}K_j$ satisfying $w_{20}\alpha_{K_0}=w_{21}C_{21}(w_{10})$, define $q_{ji,n}=w_{ji}[n]\circ s_{ji,K_i,n}$. Then
$$q_{20,n}\circ\alpha_{K_0[n]}=q_{21,n}\circ C_{21}(q_{10,n}).$$
If the $K_i$ are derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], identify ordinary and strict-tower extensions [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] by the actual quotient-map $\chi$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The same equation then holds with the specified completed normalization. In the strict cone $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, $\chi_P(z)=(c_P(z),0)$ for the family $c_P$ of quotient maps; its shift is the comparison with product coordinates $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^ny)$ [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift]. This comparison intertwines $\chi_{P[n]}$ with $\chi_P[n]$. The asserted derived identities use these comparisons and do not require a chain-level inverse to $\chi$. The conclusions include $n=0$, negative $n$, and identity coefficient extensions with their tensor multiplication and derived-completeness unit comparisons.

proof.text: Write $E_{ji}(P)=P\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ termwise. The two complexes $E_{ji}(P[n])$ and $E_{ji}(P)[n]$ have the same degree-$r$ module $P^{r+n}\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ and the same differential $(-1)^n(d_P\otimes1)$. Thus the identity in every degree is a chain isomorphism $u_{ji,P,n}$. For every chain map $f$, both sides of its naturality square are $f^{r+n}\otimes1$ in degree $r$. These identities respect homotopies: a shifted homotopy is $(-1)^n$ times the reindexed original homotopy, and termwise tensor preserves that formula. Hence $u$ is natural on homotopy categories as well. All statements use the sheafified tensor construction; they assert equality of module-sheaf maps, not an identification of tensor sheaves with sectionwise tensors.

proof.text: Flat terms remain flat after reindexing. To check K-flatness of $P[n]$, let $A$ be an acyclic test complex. On the summand with test degree $a$, multiplication by $(-1)^{na}$ identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P[n])$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P)[n]$. The differential formula in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] verifies this: the first differential gains $(-1)^n$ from the change of test degree, while the second already gains $(-1)^n$ from $P[n]$. The latter total complex is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$ and reindexing cohomology. Thus the full subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes is stable under every integer shift.

source.place: Tag 011G, homology-definition-shift-cochain; K-flat definition in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 06YL.

proof.text: Work with the small skeleton in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the coefficient universe enlarged as specified there. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes localized at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R_i)$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] the functors $E_{ji}$ followed by localization invert those quasi-isomorphisms and compute $C_{ji}$. The natural isomorphism $u$ of Step 1 consequently descends by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to $s_{ji,K,n}$. Step 2 ensures that the representative of $K[n]$ is the actual complex $P[n]$. Naturality holds for every derived morphism, since the descended transformation is natural on the localization: naturality for an inverted quasi-isomorphism is obtained by multiplying the original naturality equation by its inverses. The localization's full faithfulness makes the result independent of choices, and it preserves the zero and successive-shift identities of the identity-component maps.

proof.text:
For a flat-term K-flat $P$, [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] makes $E_{10}P$ another such representative, now over $R_1$. Therefore [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] represents the specified $\alpha$ by $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto p\otimes ab$. In degree $r$, both routes around the proposed shift/associator square send $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)$, with $p\in P^{r+n}$, to $p\otimes ab$. The shift maps insert no sign on these components, so the maps agree. The cited associator formula is a map of sheaves with the stated inverse; equality on its local tensor generators gives equality of sheaf maps. By the localization equivalence and the faithfulness clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], equality on all these representatives proves
$$s_{20,K,n}\alpha_{K[n]}=\alpha_K[n]s_{21,C_{10}K,n}C_{21}(s_{10,K,n})$$
for every $K$.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat) and 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); explicit balanced tensor calculation with Tag 011G shifts.

proof.text:
Substitute the just-proved associator square into $q_{20,n}\alpha_{K_0[n]}$. Shifting the assumed equation on $w$ and using naturality of $s_{21}$ for the derived morphism $w_{10}:C_{10}K_0\to K_1$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
q_{20,n}\alpha_{K_0[n]}&=(w_{20}\alpha_{K_0})[n]s_{21,C_{10}K_0,n}C_{21}(s_{10,K_0,n})\\
&=w_{21}[n]C_{21}(w_{10})[n]s_{21,C_{10}K_0,n}C_{21}(s_{10,K_0,n})\\
&=w_{21}[n]s_{21,K_1,n}C_{21}(w_{10}[n])C_{21}(s_{10,K_0,n})\\
&=q_{21,n}C_{21}(q_{10,n}).
\end{aligned}$$
This is a calculation with functors and composition using Steps 3--4 and the hypothesis on $w$. In particular $w$ need not lift to chain isomorphisms, and no rank-one assumption on the $K_i$ was used.

proof.text: Let $I_{ji}$ be the strict-tower extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. On a representative $P$, its quotient maps form a strictly compatible family $c_P$, so $(1-s)c_P=0$ and the specified map is $\chi_P(z)=(c_P(z),0)$. Apply [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift] with its fixed product-shift comparison. The resulting chain shift $I_{ji}(P[n])\to I_{ji}(P)[n]$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^ny)$, with degree reindexing understood. The cited theorem gives its coherence and its compatibility with the actual quotient map. In coordinates that compatibility is visible directly: the image of $\chi_{P[n]}(z)$ is $(c_{P[n]}(z),0)$, which equals $\chi_P[n](u_{ji,P,n}(z))$ because each quotient tensor shift is the identity. Thus the comparison uses the zero second coordinate of $\chi$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the two completion objects.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-completed-scalar-shift-descent], the coherent strict shift of Step 6 descends to a natural shift $t_{ji,K,n}:I_{ji}(K[n])\to I_{ji}(K)[n]$ computed on $P[n]$. Descent of the chain equation of Step 6 therefore gives
$$t_{ji,K,n}\chi_{ji,K[n]}=\chi_{ji,K}[n]s_{ji,K,n}.$$
Here [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies $\chi$ with the natural isomorphism from ordinary to strict-tower extension on derived-complete inputs, and ensures completeness of $C_{ji}K$. Completeness is stable under shift: shift the defining Roos triangle in [def-weil-derived-complete]; products and reduction maps are reindexed and the signed cone comparison of Step 6 identifies its strict realization. Thus these isomorphisms apply also to $K_i[n]$. All inverses used from now on are inverses of these isomorphisms in the derived category.

proof.text:
For complete inputs put $h_{ji}=\chi_{ji}$ and $H_K=I_{21}(h_{10,K})h_{21,C_{10}K}$. The actual completed associator $a^I$ satisfies
$$a^I_KH_K=h_{20,K}\alpha_K$$
by [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator]; its hypotheses allow arbitrary schemes and repeated fields. Set $v_{ji}=w_{ji}h_{ji,K_i}^{-1}$ and $r_{ji,n}=v_{ji}[n]t_{ji,K_i,n}$. Step 7 gives $r_{ji,n}h_{ji,K_i[n]}=q_{ji,n}$. To verify the completed tower equation, precompose with the isomorphism $H_{K_0[n]}$. The left side becomes
$$r_{20,n}a^I_{K_0[n]}H_{K_0[n]}=q_{20,n}\alpha_{K_0[n]}.$$
For the right side, functoriality and naturality of $h_{21}$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
r_{21,n}I_{21}(r_{10,n})H_{K_0[n]}
&=r_{21,n}I_{21}(q_{10,n})h_{21,C_{10}(K_0[n])}\\
&=r_{21,n}h_{21,K_1[n]}C_{21}(q_{10,n})\\
&=q_{21,n}C_{21}(q_{10,n}).
\end{aligned}$$
Step 5 identifies the results; cancel $H_{K_0[n]}$. This proves the equation for the specified completed associator and shifts, not merely an equation after arbitrary choices of objectwise identifications.

proof.text: For $n=0$, the component identities are literal identities and the cone's sign is $1$. For $n<0$, every formula above still uses the integer shift and $(-1)^n$; no induction restricted to nonnegative shifts was used. If a coefficient inclusion is an identity, ordinary change of rings has multiplication unitor $p\otimes a\mapsto ap$, which commutes with shifts since the same formula applies in degree $r+n$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] its $\chi$ is exactly the derived-completeness map under this multiplication isomorphism. The unit normalization of [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator] then gives the required completed unit identifications. The cone sign comparison still fixes the zero second coordinate, so no chain-level inverse to $\chi$ is introduced, including for identity extensions.
